hints: Focus on what sodium propanoate actually is, a three-carbon carboxylate salt, so ask which starting material can gain the C-O bonds needed for a carboxylate.
Check reactions 1 and 2 first: NaBH4 reduces an aldehyde to a primary alcohol, and Na with an alcohol gives an alkoxide plus hydrogen, neither makes a COO- group.
Now think about hot aqueous NaOH with a nitrile, recall the full hydrolysis products and see which mixture gives a three-carbon carboxylate plus ammonia.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target product**

Think like a detective. Sodium propanoate is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$. It is the sodium salt of propanoic acid.

To make it you need a reaction that creates a carboxylate group, $\text{COO}^-$, on a 3-carbon chain.

**Test mixture 1 - aldehyde + NaBH4**

$\text{NaBH}_4$ is a reducing agent. It donates hydride to carbonyls.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaBH}_4(aq)} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
This is reduction of propanal to propan-1-ol. No oxidation to acid, no carboxylate is formed, so no sodium propanoate.

**Test mixture 2 - alcohol + Na**

Alcohols are weak acids toward reactive metals. Sodium gives the alkoxide, not the carboxylate.

$$2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{H}_2$$
The product is sodium propoxide, with C-O-Na but still only one oxygen. It is not $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$.

**Test mixture 3 - nitrile + hot NaOH**

Nitriles undergo complete alkaline hydrolysis when heated under reflux with aqueous NaOH to give the carboxylate salt plus ammonia.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{NaOH}(aq) + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{NH}_3$$
This does give sodium propanoate. So only mixture 3 works.

options.A: Incorrect. It claims all three give the carboxylate. Mixture 1 stops at the primary alcohol and mixture 2 stops at the alkoxide, only the nitrile hydrolysis in 3 reaches the carboxylate oxidation level.
options.B: Incorrect. Both 1 and 2 keep the carbon at a lower oxidation state. NaBH4 is reduction, not oxidation, and Na with ROH is acid-base to give RO- Na+, neither creates the two C-O bonds of COO-.
options.C: Incorrect. While 3 is correct, 2 is not. Students often confuse sodium propoxide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{O}^-\text{Na}^+$) with sodium propanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$). The names sound similar but the functional groups are completely different.
options.D: Correct. Only 3 gives sodium propanoate. Hot alkaline hydrolysis of propanenitrile produces $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ plus $\text{NH}_3$, while 1 gives propan-1-ol and 2 gives sodium propoxide.
